lines.caption: This is a tour of the pull request for issue 150, which gives Thunar Nemo's XApp icons where it shows one-colour icons.
lines.say: This is a tour of the pull request for issue one fifty, which gives Thunar Nemo's X App icons where it shows one-colour icons.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
One helper turns an icon name into its XApp name. The toolbar, location bar and side pane try that name first.
lines.say: One helper turns an icon name into its X App name. The toolbar, location bar and side pane try that name first.

lines.caption: First, the toolbar and the location bar ask for each button's icon by name.
The side pane does the same for places, devices, bookmarks and the tree.
The helper builds the XApp name, and maps search to edit-find, since XApp has no search icon.
lines.say: The helper builds the X App name, and maps search to edit find, since X App has no search icon.

lines.caption: It then asks the icon theme whether that XApp icon is installed.
lines.say: It then asks the icon theme whether that X App icon is installed.

lines.caption: If it is, Thunar draws it in the theme's text colour, just like Nemo.
If not, Thunar draws the theme's own symbolic icon, exactly as before.
A new hidden setting turns all this on or off. It is on by default.
Toggling it refreshes the toolbar and location bar, and redraws the side pane and tree.
Thunar also watches for icon theme changes, such as icons being installed.
Those refresh only the toolbar buttons, so a path you are typing is kept.
Nemo draws its icons from the XApp set, so Thunar and Nemo looked different side by side.
lines.say: Nemo draws its icons from the X App set, so Thoonar and Nemo looked different side by side.

lines.caption: Only places that already show symbolic icons change. The main file view keeps its colour icons.
The steps below the diagram name the files behind each box, from the toolbar to the side pane.
The helper returns nothing when the setting is off, or when the theme lacks the icon.
An icon theme change refreshes only the toolbar buttons and the view switcher.
Per the issue's list, most toolbar and side pane icons have an XApp version.
lines.say: Per the issue's list, most toolbar and side pane icons have an X App version.

lines.caption: Search uses the edit-find icon, as Nemo does, and goes back to the theme's search icon when the setting is off.
lines.say: Search uses the edit find icon, as Nemo does, and goes back to the theme's search icon when the setting is off.

lines.caption: Icons missing from that list, likely the view mode buttons, keep the theme's style. That wasn't checked here.
Symlink arrows and custom action buttons are left out, because existing settings already cover them.
Here is the toolbar's change: try the XApp name first, and fall back to the theme's name.
lines.say: Here is the toolbar's change: try the X App name first, and fall back to the theme's name.

lines.caption: Ten source files change, plus the new test and this page.
To go back to the theme's icons without a new build, turn the hidden setting off with xfconf-query.
lines.say: To go back to the theme's icons without a new build, turn the hidden setting off with the X F conf query command.

lines.caption: Part 2. How it was built and verified.
Everything here ran in the building session's cloud container, with stand-in icons, since it had no XApp package.
lines.say: Everything here ran in the building session's cloud container, with stand-in icons, since it had no X App package.

lines.caption: The reference is the issue's list from the owner's Zorin machine, running Nemo with the XApp icons.
lines.say: The reference is the issue's list from the owner's Zorin machine, running Nemo with the X App icons.

lines.caption: The new setting refreshes the same way the existing symbolic icon settings do.
The test makes two stand-in icons, solid grey squares, so the change is easy to see.
The first build failed on a doc comment, which was reworded. The next two built.
On build 2, 32 of 33 tests passed. The new test failed in the side pane and in the fallback shot.
lines.say: On build two, thirty-two of thirty-three tests passed. The new test failed in the side pane and in the fallback shot.

lines.caption: The side pane now looks up the XApp icon on its own first, and the test makes GTK rescan its icons.
lines.say: The side pane now looks up the X App icon on its own first, and the test makes G T K rescan its icons.

lines.caption: On build 3, the smoke test and the new test both passed: on, off, and the fallback.
lines.say: On build three, the smoke test and the new test both passed: on, off, and the fallback.

lines.caption: The review fixes came later. They compiled cleanly but weren't run under the tests.
CI's build, tests and review run when the branch is pushed.
Not run: the real XApp package, the search icon, the location bar, and the view mode fallbacks.
lines.say: Not run: the real X App package, the search icon, the location bar, and the view mode fallbacks.

lines.caption: A local code review at high found 7 issues: 3 fixed, 3 skipped for now, and this missing page.
lines.say: A local code review at high found seven issues: three fixed, three skipped for now, and this missing page.

lines.caption: The fixes: the Search icon now switches back when the setting is off, a typed path survives a theme change, and two comments were trimmed.
Skipped: generic drive icons, a small speed cost per icon, and using the default screen's icon theme.
CI then reviews each code push, in the code review comment on the PR.
Only the owner can check the real XApp icons on Zorin, next to Nemo.
lines.say: Only the owner can check the real X App icons on Zorin, next to Nemo.

lines.caption: The issue, the branch and the test are linked here. The PR will carry CI's runs and shots.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on this one. What's left is the owner's look on the real machine.
After the merge, you compare Thunar with Nemo on Zorin, with the real XApp package.
lines.say: After the merge, you compare Thoonar with Nemo on Zorin, with the real X App package.

lines.caption: If a fallback or device icon looks out of place, that becomes a new issue.
And if you don't like it, the rollback command from Part 1 turns it off.
In short: Thunar now borrows Nemo's icons when they're installed, and keeps its theme's icons when they're not.
